title: Knowledge check: The apply() Family

questions.prompt: For “The apply() Family”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.

questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: The apply() Family is one step in Apply Functions and Functional Programming; the apply family and purrr tools help express repeated transformations; simplification rules can change result shape. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: When applying “The apply() Family” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.

questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Choose the simplest mapper that makes expected result structure obvious and test type stability. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
